name: automation/roles/upgrade/tasks/rollback.yml
review_question: Does this playbook have harmful dependency coupling?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # This playbook performs a rollback of a PostgreSQL database cluster upgrade.
     3: # It's designed to be used when a PostgreSQL upgrade hasn't been fully completed and the new version hasn't been started.
     4: # The rollback operation is performed by starting the Patroni cluster with the old version of PostgreSQL using the same PGDATA.
     5: # The playbook first checks the health of the current cluster, verifies the version of PostgreSQL, and ensures the new PostgreSQL is not running.
     6: # If these checks pass, the playbook switches back to the old PostgreSQL paths and restarts the Patroni service.
     7: # Notes:
     8: # If pg_upgrade aborted before linking started, the old cluster was unmodified; it can be restarted.
     9: # If you did not start the new cluster, the old cluster was unmodified except that,
    10: # when linking started, a .old suffix was appended to $PGDATA/global/pg_control.
    11: # To reuse the old cluster, remove the .old suffix from $PGDATA/global/pg_control; you can then restart the old cluster.
    12: # If you did start the new cluster, it has written to shared files and it is unsafe to use the old cluster.
    13: # The old cluster will need to be restored from backup in this case.
    14: 
    15: # If the cluster is already healthy, the process stops to avoid unnecessary actions.
    16: - name: "[Rollback] Check Patroni cluster state"
    17:   ansible.builtin.uri:
    18:     url: "{{ patroni_restapi_protocol }}://{{ patroni_restapi_connect_addr | default(patroni_bind_address | default(bind_address, true), true) }}:\
    19:       {{ patroni_restapi_port }}/cluster"
    20:     return_content: true
    21:     ca_path: "{{ patroni_restapi_cafile | default(omit, true) }}"
    22:   register: patroni_cluster_result
    23:   failed_when: false
    24:   changed_when: false
    25:   environment:
    26:     no_proxy: "{{ patroni_bind_address | default(bind_address, true) }}"
    27:   when:
    28:     - inventory_hostname in groups['primary']
    29: 
    30: # Stop, if the Patroni cluster is already healthy
    31: - name: "[Rollback] Abort if the Patroni cluster is already running"
    32:   ansible.builtin.fail:
    33:     msg: "The Patroni cluster is already running. Stop rollback."
    34:   vars:
    35:     cluster_members: "{{ patroni_cluster_result.json.members | default([]) | rejectattr('state', 'equalto', 'stopped') | list | length }}"
    36:     total_nodes: "{{ groups['primary'] | length + groups.get('secondary', []) | length }}"
    37:   when:
    38:     - inventory_hostname in groups['primary']
    39:     # Check if the cluster members (excluding 'stopped') equals the total number of nodes
    40:     - cluster_members == total_nodes
    41: 
    42: - name: "[Rollback] Make sure the new PostgreSQL is not running"
    43:   ansible.builtin.command: "{{ pg_new_bindir }}/pg_ctl status -D {{ pg_new_datadir }}"
    44:   register: pg_ctl_status_new_result
    45:   failed_when: false
    46:   changed_when: false
    47: 
    48: # Stop, if new PostgreSQL is running
    49: # "If you did start the new cluster, it has written to shared files and it is unsafe to use the old cluster."
    50: - name: "[Rollback] Abort if the new PostgreSQL cluster is already running"
    51:   ansible.builtin.fail:
    52:     msg:
    53:       - "The PostgreSQL {{ pg_new_version }} is running on host {{ ansible_hostname }}. We can't rollback."
    54:   when:
    55:     - pg_ctl_status_new_result is defined
    56:     - pg_ctl_status_new_result.rc == 0
    57: 
    58: - name: Check if pg_control.old exists
    59:   ansible.builtin.stat:
    60:     path: "{{ pg_old_datadir }}/global/pg_control.old"
    61:   register: pg_control_old
    62: 
    63: # if 'pg_control.old' exists
    64: # "To reuse the old cluster, remove the .old suffix from $PGDATA/global/pg_control"
    65: - name: "[Rollback] Rename pg_control.old to pg_control"
    66:   ansible.builtin.command: mv "{{ pg_old_datadir }}/global/pg_control.old" "{{ pg_old_datadir }}/global/pg_control"
    67:   when: pg_control_old.stat.exists
    68: 
    69: - name: "[Rollback] Check PostgreSQL version in pg_control"
    70:   ansible.builtin.shell: |
    71:     set -o pipefail;
    72:     {{ pg_old_bindir }}/pg_controldata {{ pg_old_datadir }} | grep 'pg_control version number' | awk '{print substr($4, 1, 2)}'
    73:   args:
    74:     executable: /bin/bash
    75:   changed_when: false
    76:   register: pg_control_version
    77:   when:
    78:     - inventory_hostname in groups['primary']
    79: 
    80: # Stop, if 'pg_control version number' is equal to the new PostgreSQL version
    81: - name: "[Rollback] Abort if the PostgreSQL version does not match expected version"
    82:   ansible.builtin.fail:
    83:     msg:
    84:       - "The version in pg_control ({{ pg_control_version.stdout }}) is not equal to the PostgreSQL {{ pg_old_version }}. We can't rollback."
    85:       - "The old cluster will need to be restored from backup."
    86:   when:
    87:     - inventory_hostname in groups['primary']
    88:     - pg_control_version.stdout == pg_new_version | string | replace('.', '')
    89: 
    90: # Restore the old Patroni configuration
    91: - name: "[Rollback] Restore the old patroni.yml configuration file"
    92:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    93:     src: "{{ patroni_config_file }}.bkp"
    94:     dest: "{{ patroni_config_file }}"
    95:     owner: postgres
    96:     group: postgres
    97:     mode: "0640"
    98:     remote_src: true
    99: 
   100: - name: "[Rollback] Ensure old PostgreSQL paths are set in patroni.yml"
   101:   ansible.builtin.replace:
   102:     path: "{{ patroni_config_file }}"
   103:     regexp: "{{ item.regexp }}"
   104:     replace: "{{ item.replace }}"
   105:   loop:
   106:     - { regexp: "data_dir: {{ pg_new_datadir }}", replace: "data_dir: {{ pg_old_datadir }}" }
   107:     - { regexp: "bin_dir: {{ pg_new_bindir }}", replace: "bin_dir: {{ pg_old_bindir }}" }
   108:     - { regexp: "config_dir: {{ pg_new_confdir }}", replace: "config_dir: {{ pg_old_confdir }}" }
   109:   loop_control:
   110:     label: "{{ item.replace }}"
   111: 
   112: # Start Patroni cluster
   113: - name: "[Rollback] Start Patroni service on the cluster leader"
   114:   become: true
   115:   become_user: root
   116:   ansible.builtin.service:
   117:     name: patroni
   118:     state: started
   119:   when:
   120:     - inventory_hostname in groups['primary']
   121: 
   122: - name: "[Rollback] Wait for port {{ patroni_restapi_port | default('8008') }} to become open on the host"
   123:   ansible.builtin.wait_for:
   124:     port: "{{ patroni_restapi_port }}"
   125:     host: "{{ patroni_bind_address | default(bind_address, true) }}"
   126:     state: started
   127:     timeout: "{{ (pg_start_stop_timeout | int) // 2 }}"
   128:     delay: 2
   129:   when:
   130:     - inventory_hostname in groups['primary']
   131: 
   132: - name: "[Rollback] Resume Patroni (disable maintenance mode)"
   133:   run_once: true
   134:   ansible.builtin.command: "patronictl -c {{ patroni_config_file }} resume --wait {{ patroni_cluster_name }}"
   135:   environment:
   136:     PATH: "{{ ansible_env.PATH }}:/usr/bin:/usr/local/bin"
   137:   failed_when: false
   138: 
   139: - name: "[Rollback] Check Patroni is healthy on the leader"
   140:   ansible.builtin.uri:
   141:     url: "{{ patroni_restapi_protocol }}://{{ patroni_restapi_connect_addr | default(patroni_bind_address | default(bind_address, true), true) }}:\
   142:       {{ patroni_restapi_port }}/leader"
   143:     status_code: 200
   144:     ca_path: "{{ patroni_restapi_cafile | default(omit, true) }}"
   145:   register: patroni_leader_result
   146:   until: patroni_leader_result.status == 200
   147:   retries: "{{ (pg_start_stop_timeout | int) // 2 }}"
   148:   delay: 2
   149:   environment:
   150:     no_proxy: "{{ patroni_bind_address | default(bind_address, true) }}"
   151:   when:
   152:     - inventory_hostname in groups['primary']
   153: 
   154: - name: "[Rollback] Start Patroni service on the cluster replica"
   155:   become: true
   156:   become_user: root
   157:   ansible.builtin.service:
   158:     name: patroni
   159:     state: started
   160:   when:
   161:     - inventory_hostname in groups.get('secondary', [])
   162: 
   163: - name: "[Rollback] Wait for port {{ patroni_restapi_port | default('8008') }} to become open on the host"
   164:   ansible.builtin.wait_for:
   165:     port: "{{ patroni_restapi_port }}"
   166:     host: "{{ patroni_bind_address | default(bind_address, true) }}"
   167:     state: started
   168:     timeout: "{{ (pg_start_stop_timeout | int) // 2 }}"
   169:     delay: 2
   170:   when:
   171:     - inventory_hostname in groups.get('secondary', [])
   172: 
   173: - name: "[Rollback] Check Patroni is healthy on the replica"
   174:   ansible.builtin.uri:
   175:     url: "{{ patroni_restapi_protocol }}://{{ patroni_restapi_connect_addr | default(patroni_bind_address | default(bind_address, true), true) }}:\
   176:       {{ patroni_restapi_port }}/health"
   177:     status_code: 200
   178:     ca_path: "{{ patroni_restapi_cafile | default(omit, true) }}"
   179:   register: patroni_replica_result

   181:   retries: "{{ (pg_start_stop_timeout | int) // 2 }}"
   182:   delay: 2
   183:   environment:
   184:     no_proxy: "{{ patroni_bind_address | default(bind_address, true) }}"
   185:   when:
   186:     - inventory_hostname in groups.get('secondary', [])
   187: 
   188: # if 'pgbouncer_install' is 'true' and 'pgbouncer_pool_pause' is 'true'
   189: - block:

    19: 
    20:   pre_tasks:
    21:     - name: Validate required variables are populated
    22:       ansible.builtin.assert:
    23:         that:
    24:           - wireguard_peer_pubkey | length > 0
    25:           - cape_api_key | length > 0
    26:           - bazaar_auth_key | length > 0
    27:         fail_msg: |
    28:           One or more required variables are empty:

    30:             cape_api_key          — Cape API token (ansible/vars/secrets.yml)

    33:     # Separate from the block above, and tagged `always`, because the assert above
    34:     # does NOT run on a tagged deploy — and a key rotation is exactly a tagged deploy
    35:     # (make deploy TAGS=litellm,api,interpret,ntfy-alerts). Two gaps compound there:
    36:     # pre_tasks are skipped unless tagged `always`, and `| mandatory` at the call
    37:     # sites fires only on UNDEFINED, not on empty. Without this, a rotation with an
    38:     # unfilled vault entry renders master_key: "" into LiteLLM's config and reports
    39:     # success — the same silently-passing guard as #238 itself.
    40:     #
    41:     # Scoped to this one variable rather than tagging the whole block, so tagged
    42:     # workflows that tolerate an empty optional secret keep working.
    43:     - name: Validate the LiteLLM master key (runs on tagged deploys too)

    55:       tags: [always]
    56: 
    57:     # --- Deploy provenance (#151) ------------------------------------------
    58:     #
    59:     # Tagged `always` for exactly the reason the assert above is: a TAGGED deploy is
    60:     # when drift happens, and pre_tasks are skipped unless tagged. `make deploy
    61:     # TAGS=pipeline` is the common case, so a provenance marker that only appeared on
    62:     # full deploys would be absent precisely when it is needed.
    63:     #
    64:     # Records BRANCH and DIRTY, not just the SHA. On 2026-08-03 a `TAGS=pipeline`
    65:     # deploy ran from a clean `main` while the change under test (the qwen@15 arm)
    66:     # existed only on a feature branch. The host silently reverted to main's copy and
    67:     # the next eval would have run at the wrong depth for 50 minutes. A bare SHA would
    68:     # have looked perfectly healthy — main was clean and current. What was needed was
    69:     # the ability to ask "is THIS commit live?", which `make provenance` now answers.

    71:     # anyway, and ansible-lint's run-once[task] rule rejects it as
    72:     # strategy-dependent. The git reads are idempotent regardless.
    73:     - name: Read the deploying checkout's git HEAD

    75:         cmd: git rev-parse HEAD

    78:       changed_when: false
    79:       delegate_to: localhost
    80:       become: false
    81:       tags: [always]
    82: 
    83:     - name: Read the deploying checkout's branch

    93:     # Uncommitted changes mean the deployed bytes correspond to NO commit, so the SHA

    99:         cmd: git status --porcelain

   105:       tags: [always]
   106:

   125:       tags: [always]

   127:     # STARTED, not deployed. This runs before a single role, so it records what

    44:       /tmp/dcenter_dhcp_config/dhcpd{,6}_ldap.conf r,
    45:       /tmp/dcenter_dhcp_config/dhcpd{,6}.leases* lrw,
    46:       /tmp/dcenter_dhcp_config/dhcpd{,6}.pid rw,
    47:     mode: "0644"
    48:

    50:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    51:     dest: "/etc/apparmor.d/local/usr.sbin.named"
    52:     content: |
    53:       /tmp/dcenter_dhcp_config/named.conf r,
    54:       /tmp/dcenter_dhcp_config/named.zone r,
    55:       /tmp/dcenter_dhcp_config/named.pid w,
    56:     mode: "0644"
    57: 
    58: - name: Add dcenter-specific NFS overrides to /etc/nfs.conf.d/12-delphix-dcenter-nfs-overrides.conf
    59:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    60:     src: etc/
    61:     dest: /etc/
    62:     owner: root
    63:     group: root
    64:     mode: "0444"

    66: - name: Mask named and dhcp services
    67:   ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
    68:     name: "{{ item }}"

   377:   # whether it is running now — every VDI guest publishes started = false while

   410: # overall ansible-playbook exit code non-zero again when that happened, so
   411: # CI/cron/exit-code monitoring is never silently green on a real failure.
   412: # =============================================================================

   414: # =============================================================================

   417: # no state — a rebuild is a re-publish.
   418: #
   419: # `static_site_source_dir` is intentionally not set here. It is a control-node
   420: # path whose contents are never committed to this repo, so it is supplied at
   421: # converge time (`-e static_site_source_dir=...`); the role fails loudly when
   422: # it is missing rather than publishing an empty document root.
   423: # =============================================================================
   424: 
   425: - name: Serve a static document root

   427:   become: true
   428:   tags:
   429:     - static_site
   430:     - web
   431:   roles:

source_context:
1: ---
     2: # =============================================================================
     3: # Phase 0: APT Cache Infrastructure
     4: # apt-cacher-ng must be deployed BEFORE any roles that install apt packages
     5: # =============================================================================
     6: 
     7: - name: Deploy apt-cacher-ng caching proxy
     8:   hosts: apt_cacher_group
     9:   become: true
    10:   gather_facts: true
    11:   tags:
    12:     - apt_cacher_ng
    13:     - apt_proxy
    14:     - lxc
    15:   roles:
    16:     - role: apt_cacher_ng
    17: 
    18: - name: Configure apt proxy on LXC containers
    19:   hosts: lxc_containers:!apt_cacher_group:!download_vpn_group
    20:   become: true
    21:   gather_facts: false
    22:   tags:
    23:     - apt_proxy
    24:     - lxc
    25:   tasks:
    26:     # The cache is an HA pair (tofu node_services generates one instance per
    27:     # always-on node; all carry the `apt-cache` tag, so apt_cacher_group tracks
    28:     # them with no inventory change here). apt itself supports only a single
    29:     # Acquire::http::Proxy value, so instance selection uses apt's native
    30:     # Proxy-Auto-Detect hook instead: at every apt run the script probes each
    31:     # instance by FQDN and prints the first live one, or DIRECT so apt fails
    32:     # open when the whole pool is down. An instance (or its node) going down
    33:     # therefore costs one probe timeout, never apt itself.
    34:     - name: Deploy apt proxy autodetect script
    35:       when: groups['apt_cacher_group'] | default([]) | length > 0
    36:       vars:
    37:         _apt_cache_port: >-
    38:           {{ tofu_data.constants.service_ports.apt_cacher_ng
    39:              | default(3142) }}
    40:       ansible.builtin.copy:
    41:         dest: /usr/local/bin/apt-proxy-detect
    42:         content: |
    43:           #!/bin/bash
    44:           # Managed by Ansible (ansible-proxmox-apps site.yml) — do not edit.
    45:           # apt Acquire::http::Proxy-Auto-Detect hook: first live cache wins,
    46:           # DIRECT when none answer (fail open, apt fetches upstream).
    47:           for host in {% for h in groups['apt_cacher_group'] | sort -%}
    48:           {{ h }}.{{ tofu_data.domain }} {% endfor %}; do
    49:             if timeout 2 bash -c "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/${host}/{{ _apt_cache_port }}" 2>/dev/null; then
    50:               exec 3>&- 2>/dev/null
    51:               echo "http://${host}:{{ _apt_cache_port }}"
    52:               exit 0
    53:             fi
    54:           done
    55:           echo DIRECT
    56:         owner: root
    57:         group: root
    58:         mode: '0755'
    59: 
    60:     - name: Configure apt proxy
    61:       when: groups['apt_cacher_group'] | default([]) | length > 0
    62:       ansible.builtin.copy:
    63:         dest: /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/00proxy
    64:         content: |
    65:           Acquire::http::Proxy-Auto-Detect "/usr/local/bin/apt-proxy-detect";
    66:         owner: root
    67:         group: root
    68:         mode: '0644'
    69: 
    70:     - name: Remove stale apt proxy configuration
    71:       when: groups['apt_cacher_group'] | default([]) | length == 0
    72:       ansible.builtin.file:
    73:         path: "{{ item }}"
    74:         state: absent
    75:       loop:
    76:         - /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/00proxy
    77:         - /usr/local/bin/apt-proxy-detect
    78: 
    79: 
    80: # =============================================================================
    81: # Phase 0-zot: Zot OCI Registry
    82: # Self-hosted pull-through cache (docker.io/ghcr.io/quay.io) and private
    83: # registry. Deployed early — before any docker app roles — so firewalled
    84: # docker hosts can pull through it. Pairs with the tofu registry LXC 109.

    90:   gather_facts: true
    91:   tags:
    92:     - zot
    93:     - registry
    94:     - lxc

    96:     - role: zot_registry

    98: - name: Configure Docker registry mirror on LXC containers
    99:   hosts: lxc_containers:!registry_group
   100:   become: true
   101:   gather_facts: false
   102:   tags:
   103:     - registry_mirror
   104:     - docker
   105:     - lxc
   106:   handlers:
   107:     - name: Restart docker

   109:         name: docker
   110:         state: restarted
   111:   tasks:
   112:     # This play is the single owner of /etc/docker/daemon.json on docker LXCs.

   114:     # on a separate branch) to avoid two writers fighting over the same file.
   115:     - name: Configure Docker registry mirror

   117:         - "'registry' in hostvars"
   118:         - "'docker' in (host_tags | default([]))"
   119:       vars:
   120:         _registry_ip: "{{ hostvars['registry']['container_ip'] }}"
   121:         _registry_port: >-
   122:           {{ hostvars['localhost']['tofu_data']
   123:              ['constants']['service_ports']['registry']
   124:              | default(5000) }}
   125:       ansible.builtin.copy:
   126:         dest: /etc/docker/daemon.json
   127:         content: |
   128:           {
   129:             "registry-mirrors": ["http://{{ _registry_ip }}:{{ _registry_port }}"],
   130:             "insecure-registries": ["{{ _registry_ip }}:{{ _registry_port }}"],
   131:             "storage-driver": "fuse-overlayfs",
   132:             "log-driver": "journald"
   133:           }
   134:         owner: root
   135:         group: root
   136:         mode: '0644'
   137:       notify: Restart docker
   138: 
   139: # =============================================================================
   140: # Phase 0a: NTP Time Synchronization Baseline
   141: # Runs after apt-cacher-ng is up and the apt proxy is configured, so LXC
   142: # containers with outbound-internal firewall (cribl_edge, cribl_stream)
   143: # can install chrony via the proxy. Establishes accurate time on every
   144: # managed VM/container before anything that depends on it (TLS handshakes,
   145: # log timestamps, certificate validation, Splunk _time correlation).
   146: # Points at the Proxmox hosts (stratum-2 servers managed by ansible-proxmox)
   147: # when PROXMOX_NTP_SERVERS is set in Doppler; falls back to the Debian
   148: # public pool when not.
   149: # =============================================================================
   150: 
   151: - name: Configure NTP time synchronization baseline
   152:   hosts: all:!localhost
   153:   become: true
   154:   gather_facts: true
   155:   tags:
   156:     - ntp
   157:     - time
   158:     - baseline
   159:   roles:
   160:     - role: ntp
   161: 
   162: # =============================================================================
   163: # Phase 0a1b: OpenBao SSH client-CA trust on VMs (ssh-certificate-authority
   164: # ADR). SSH-reached guests only — LXCs get the same trust from ansible-proxmox
   165: # (pct push, no SSH chicken-and-egg). Runs after NTP: certificate validity is
   166: # time-bound and the role preflights clock sync. Pinned-fingerprint fetch,
   167: # fail-closed; static keys stay as break-glass until the WS4 rotation.
   168: # =============================================================================
   169: 
   170: - name: Trust the OpenBao SSH client CA on VMs
   171:   hosts: vms:splunk_vms:docker_vms

   173:   gather_facts: true
   174:   tags:
   175:     - ssh_ca_trust
   176:     - baseline
   177:   roles:
   178:     - role: ssh_ca_trust
   179: 
   180: # =============================================================================
   181: # Phase 0a2: Syslog forwarding to the central pipeline
   182: # Every infra LXC ships its logs (systemd journal + native services) to the
   183: # HAProxy syslog VIP -> Cribl Edge -> Splunk (os index). Runs after NTP so log
   184: # timestamps are accurate. The pipeline (cribl_edge / cribl_stream) and the load
   185: # balancer (haproxy) are excluded: they RECEIVE this traffic, so forwarding into

   187: #
   188: # iac-platform (the docker_vms member running Semaphore) is added explicitly

   190: # testing/dev only and stays off the production pipeline.
   191: # =============================================================================
   192: 
   193: - name: Forward infra LXC (and iac-platform) logs to the syslog pipeline
   194:   hosts: lxc_containers:!cribl_edge:!cribl_stream_group:!haproxy_group:iac-platform
   195:   become: true
   196:   gather_facts: false
   197:   tags:
   198:     - syslog_forwarder
   199:     - logging
   200:     - baseline
   201:   roles:
   202:     - role: syslog_forwarder
   203: 
   204: # =============================================================================
   205: # Phase 0b: Object Storage

   207: # =============================================================================
   208: 
   209: - name: Deploy RustFS object storage
   210:   hosts: object_storage_group
   211:   become: true
   212:   gather_facts: false
   213:   tags:
   214:     - object-storage
   215:     - storage

   217:     - role: object_storage

   222: # gather_facts is true here, unlike the storage play above: the role selects

   226: - name: Deploy Proxmox Backup Server

1: ---
     2: # Create tagged, IP-less VM bridges on the TrueNAS spare trunk port.
     3: # Additive and zero-downtime: the primary interface (enp2s0f0), its host
     4: # IPs, and the docker macvlan networks are never touched.
     5: #
     6: # Topology: truenas_vm_trunk_parent (enp1s0f0) is cabled to a tagged-only
     7: # switch trunk (crs317 sfp-sfpplus13, frame-types admit-only-vlan-tagged;
     8: # 1G module for now). For each entry in truenas_vm_bridges this play
     9: # creates vlan<tag>@trunk and a host bridge enslaving it, with NO host
    10: # IPs — pure L2 for VM taps. VM<->host traffic (e.g. the democratic-csi
    11: # portal at 10.10.9.213) hairpins through the switch between the trunk
    12: # port and the primary port: standard two-port forwarding.
    13: #
    14: # STP is disabled on these bridges: a single-member edge bridge cannot
    15: # form a loop, and the Linux STP listening/learning delay (~30s) on
    16: # newly-attached VM tap ports can outlast an iPXE DHCP window.
    17: #
    18: # Safety: uses the TrueNAS stage -> commit(rollback) -> checkin flow, and
    19: # the post-commit state is verified BEFORE interface.checkin — an assert
    20: # failure aborts the play inside the rollback window, so TrueNAS reverts
    21: # the change on its own at checkin_timeout. No host IPs move, so SSH
    22: # stays up throughout.
    23: #
    24: # Idempotent and health-checking: a converged re-run stages nothing but
    25: # still asserts the trunk link, the bare-L2 invariant, and that every
    26: # bridge/VLAN pair exists.
    27: #
    28: # Variables (igou-inventory group_vars/truenas.yml):
    29: #   truenas_vm_trunk_parent — spare physical NIC cabled to the tagged trunk
    30: #   truenas_vm_bridges      — list of {name, vlan_name, vlan_tag}

    33:   hosts: truenas
    34:   gather_facts: false
    35:   become: false
    36: 
    37:   tasks:
    38: 
    39:     - name: Assert trunk and bridge variables are defined
    40:       ansible.builtin.assert:
    41:         that:
    42:           - truenas_vm_trunk_parent is defined
    43:           - truenas_vm_bridges | default([]) | length > 0
    44:         fail_msg: >-
    45:           truenas_vm_trunk_parent / truenas_vm_bridges are missing — define

    62:         _missing_vlans: "{{ truenas_vm_bridges | rejectattr('vlan_name', 'in', _iface_names) | list }}"

    90:     - name: Probe trunk link state (up to 10s)
    91:       ansible.builtin.command:
    92:         argv:
    93:           - midclt
    94:           - call
    95:           - interface.query
    96:           - '[["name", "=", "{{ truenas_vm_trunk_parent }}"]]'
    97:       register: _trunk_probe
    98:       changed_when: false
    99:       failed_when: false
   100:       retries: 5
   101:       delay: 2
   102:       until: >-
   103:         ((_trunk_probe.stdout | from_json | first | default({})).state
   104:          | default({})).link_state | default('') == 'LINK_STATE_UP'
   105: 
   106:     - name: Assert the trunk parent has link (cable present)
   107:       ansible.builtin.assert:
   108:         that: (_trunk_probe.stdout | from_json | first).state.link_state == 'LINK_STATE_UP'
   109:         fail_msg: >-
   110:           {{ truenas_vm_trunk_parent }} has no link — check the cable/module to
   111:           the tagged switch trunk port (crs317 sfp-sfpplus13) and confirm the
   112:           switch config is deployed before running this play.
   113: 
   114:     - name: Assert the trunk parent is a bare L2 port (no IPs, no DHCP/SLAAC)
   115:       ansible.builtin.assert:
   116:         that:
   117:           - _trunk[0].aliases | length == 0
   118:           - not _trunk[0].ipv4_dhcp
   119:           - not _trunk[0].ipv6_auto
   120:         fail_msg: >-
   121:           {{ truenas_vm_trunk_parent }} has IP configuration — refusing. This
   122:           play only manages a bare tagged trunk; move or remove the IPs first.
   123: 
   124:     - name: Refuse to run with pending uncommitted interface changes
   125:       ansible.builtin.command:
   126:         argv: [midclt, call, interface.has_pending_changes]
   127:       register: _pending
   128:       changed_when: false
   129:       # midclt prints Python-style booleans here ("False"), not JSON
   130:       failed_when: _pending.stdout | trim | lower != 'false'
   131:       when: _changes_needed
   132: 
   133:     - name: Stage VLAN sub-interfaces on the trunk
   134:       ansible.builtin.command:
   135:         argv:
   136:           - midclt
   137:           - call
   138:           - interface.create
   139:           - >-
   140:             {{ {'name': item.vlan_name,
   141:                 'type': 'VLAN',
   142:                 'description': 'VM trunk VLAN ' ~ item.vlan_tag
   143:                                ~ ' (' ~ truenas_vm_trunk_parent ~ ')',
   144:                 'vlan_parent_interface': truenas_vm_trunk_parent,
   145:                 'vlan_tag': item.vlan_tag} | to_json }}
   146:       loop: "{{ _missing_vlans }}"
   147:       loop_control:
   148:         label: "{{ item.vlan_name }}"
   149:       changed_when: true
   150: 
   151:     - name: Stage IP-less bridges enslaving the VLAN sub-interfaces
   152:       ansible.builtin.command:
   153:         argv:
   154:           - midclt
   155:           - call
   156:           - interface.create
   157:           - >-
   158:             {{ {'name': item.name,
   159:                 'type': 'BRIDGE',
   160:                 'description': 'VM bridge (tagged VLAN ' ~ item.vlan_tag
   161:                                ~ ' via ' ~ truenas_vm_trunk_parent ~ ', no host IPs)',
   162:                 'bridge_members': [item.vlan_name],
   163:                 'stp': false} | to_json }}
   164:       loop: "{{ _missing_bridges }}"
   165:       loop_control:
   166:         label: "{{ item.name }}"
   167:       changed_when: true
   168: 
   169:     - name: Commit staged changes (no host IPs move — SSH stays up)
   170:       ansible.builtin.command:
   171:         argv:
   172:           - midclt
   173:           - call
   174:           - interface.commit
   175:           - '{"rollback": true, "checkin_timeout": 60}'
   176:       changed_when: true
   177:       when: _changes_needed
   178: 
   179:     - name: Query interfaces after commit
   180:       ansible.builtin.command:
   181:         argv: [midclt, call, interface.query]
   182:       register: _postquery
   183:       changed_when: false
   184: 
   185:     - name: Assert every VM bridge and VLAN sub-interface exists
   186:       vars:
   187:         _post_names: "{{ _postquery.stdout | from_json | map(attribute='name') | list }}"
   188:       ansible.builtin.assert:
   189:         that:
   190:           - item.name in _post_names
   191:           - item.vlan_name in _post_names
   192:         fail_msg: >-
   193:           {{ item.name }}/{{ item.vlan_name }} missing after commit — aborting
   194:           before checkin so the pending change auto-rolls back at
   195:           checkin_timeout; check `midclt call interface.query` and the
   196:           middleware log.
   197:       loop: "{{ truenas_vm_bridges }}"
   198:       loop_control:
   199:         label: "{{ item.name }}"
   200: 
   201:     - name: Check in — persist the verified changes
   202:       ansible.builtin.command:
   203:         argv: [midclt, call, interface.checkin]
   204:       changed_when: true
   205:       when: _changes_needed
   206: 
   207:     - name: Report next steps
   208:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   209:         msg: >-
   210:           Tagged VM bridge(s) ready:
   211:           {{ truenas_vm_bridges | map(attribute='name') | list }}. Next: run
   212:           configure_vms.yaml. The L2 path proves itself end-to-end when a VM
   213:           PXE-boots (DHCP from rb5009 arrives via the trunk).

name: playbooks/rpi_netboot/stage_netboot_assets.yml
review_question: Does this playbook have harmful dependency coupling?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Per-Pi netboot staging: netboot server first, then the router.
     3: #   1. rpis group: resolve contract + TFTP prefix + rootfs src per host.
     4: #   2. netboot_server group: rpi_rootfs role per managed Pi (NFS rootfs
     5: #      + full boot-partition TFTP staging), then fetch each Pi's shared
     6: #      boot assets (firmware/kernel/dtb) to the controller cache.
     7: #   3. rpis group (serial): upload the shared <model>/<build_id> set to
     8: #      the router's flash once (size-gated dedup across Pis on the same
     9: #      build) and register this Pi's per-prefix /ip tftp rows pointing
    10: #      into it. Pin files (config.txt/cmdline.txt) are owned by
    11: #      converge_boot_mode.yml, not staged here.
    12: #
    13: # Scope with -e rpi_group=<group> — not --limit. The plays mix rpis
    14: # with netboot_server, and play 2 loops over the rpis group from the
    15: # netboot_server host, so --limit silently empties it.
    16: - name: Resolve per-Pi config and rootfs sources
    17:   hosts: "{{ rpi_group | default('rpis') }}"
    18:   gather_facts: false
    19:   tasks:
    20:     - name: Resolve effective rpi config
    21:       ansible.builtin.include_tasks: tasks/_resolve_rpi_config.yml
    22: 
    23:     - name: Resolve rpi_rootfs_src per host
    24:       ansible.builtin.include_tasks: tasks/_resolve_rootfs_src.yml
    25:       when: rpi_netboot_managed
    26: 
    27: - name: Provision per-Pi NFS rootfs + stage and fetch boot assets
    28:   hosts: "{{ rpi_netboot_server_group | default('netboot_server') }}"
    29:   become: true
    30:   gather_facts: false
    31:   vars:
    32:     _managed_pis: >-
    33:       {{ groups[rpi_group | default('rpis')]
    34:          | map('extract', hostvars)
    35:          | selectattr('rpi_netboot_managed', 'defined')
    36:          | selectattr('rpi_netboot_managed')
    37:          | map(attribute='inventory_hostname') | list }}
    38:     # (host, asset) cross-product for the fetch loop. Built with
    39:     # targeted attribute access only: piping full hostvars dicts through
    40:     # subelements() forces EVERY inherited var to render, and fact-less
    41:     # plays then explode on unrelated vars that template ansible_facts
    42:     # (baseline_user_groups' os_family lookup, first hit at the bench).
    43:     _fetch_pairs: >-
    44:       {%- set out = [] -%}
    45:       {%- for h in _managed_pis -%}
    46:       {%-   for a in hostvars[h].rpi_tftp_assets -%}
    47:       {%-     set _ = out.append({'host': h,
    48:                                   'cache_dir': hostvars[h].rpi_tftp_cache_dir,
    49:                                   'asset': a}) -%}
    50:       {%-   endfor -%}
    51:       {%- endfor -%}
    52:       {{ out }}
    53:   tasks:
    54:     - name: Run rpi_rootfs per Pi
    55:       ansible.builtin.include_role:
    56:         name: rpi_rootfs
    57:       vars:
    58:         rpi_rootfs_src: "{{ hostvars[_pi].rpi_rootfs_src }}"
    59:         rpi_rootfs_src_sha256: "{{ hostvars[_pi].rpi_rootfs_src_sha256 | default('') }}"
    60:         rpi_rootfs_host: "{{ _pi }}"
    61:         rpi_rootfs_force_refresh: "{{ rpi_force_refresh | default(false) }}"
    62:       loop: "{{ _managed_pis }}"
    63:       loop_control:
    64:         loop_var: _pi
    65: 
    66:     - name: Ensure controller cache dir exists per host
    67:       ansible.builtin.file:
    68:         path: "{{ hostvars[item].rpi_tftp_cache_dir }}/{{ item }}"
    69:         state: directory
    70:         mode: "0755"
    71:       delegate_to: localhost
    72:       # Force a real local connection: inventory `localhost` defaults to
    73:       # SSH (it is an SSH-able build host), and this devcontainer's sshd
    74:       # has PrivateTmp, so an SSH-delegated mkdir creates a private /tmp
    75:       # the fetch below (controller-side write) cannot see.
    76:       vars:
    77:         ansible_connection: local
    78:       become: false
    79:       loop: "{{ _managed_pis }}"
    80: 
    81:     - name: Fetch each (host, asset) pair from netboot server
    82:       ansible.builtin.fetch:
    83:         src: "{{ rpi_image_cache }}/rpi-tftp/{{ item.host }}/{{ item.asset }}"
    84:         dest: "{{ item.cache_dir }}/{{ item.host }}/{{ item.asset }}"
    85:         flat: true
    86:       loop: "{{ _fetch_pairs }}"
    87:       loop_control:
    88:         label: "{{ item.host }}/{{ item.asset }}"
    89: 
    90: - name: Upload shared TFTP assets to router and register per-Pi rows
    91:   hosts: "{{ rpi_group | default('rpis') }}"
    92:   gather_facts: false
    93:   # One Pi at a time: every host's uploads delegate to the same router,
    94:   # and parallel net_put bursts flake RouterOS's SSH server.
    95:   serial: 1
    96:   vars:
    97:     _shared_dir: "{{ rpi_tftp_flash_dir }}/shared/{{ rpi_board_model }}/{{ rpi_build_id }}"
    98:     # Every build still referenced by a managed Pi of this model — the
    99:     # prune step below must not delete a sibling Pi's active build.
   100:     _active_builds: >-
   101:       {{ groups[rpi_group | default('rpis')]
   102:          | map('extract', hostvars)
   103:          | selectattr('rpi_netboot_managed', 'defined')
   104:          | selectattr('rpi_netboot_managed')
   105:          | selectattr('rpi_board_model', 'equalto', rpi_board_model)
   106:          | map(attribute='rpi_build_id') | unique | list }}
   107:   tasks:
   108:     - name: Stage this Pi's assets on the router
   109:       delegate_to: "{{ rpi_router }}"
   110:       when: rpi_netboot_managed
   111:       block:
   112:         - name: Assert the TFTP prefix is derivable
   113:           ansible.builtin.include_tasks: transport/assert_tftp_prefix.yml
   114: 
   115:         - name: Ensure shared dir hierarchy exists on router flash
   116:           community.routeros.command:
   117:             commands:
   118:               - >-
   119:                 :if ([/file find name="{{ item }}" type=directory] = "")
   120:                 do={/file add name="{{ item }}" type=directory}
   121:           register: _shareddir
   122:           retries: 3
   123:           delay: 5
   124:           until: _shareddir is succeeded
   125:           changed_when: false
   126:           loop:
   127:             - "{{ rpi_tftp_flash_dir }}/shared"
   128:             - "{{ rpi_tftp_flash_dir }}/shared/{{ rpi_board_model }}"
   129:             - "{{ _shared_dir }}"
   130: 
   131:         - name: Retarget this Pi's rows onto the current build dir
   132:           ansible.builtin.include_tasks: transport/retarget_tftp_row.yml
   133:           vars:
   134:             _retarget_req: "{{ rpi_tftp_prefix }}/{{ item }}"
   135:             _retarget_real: "{{ _shared_dir }}/{{ item }}"
   136:           loop: "{{ rpi_tftp_assets }}"
   137: 
   138:         - name: Upload each shared asset + register this Pi's row
   139:           # Reuses the armbian domain's generic size-gated primitive —
   140:           # it only consumes _upload_* vars. The shared path is keyed by
   141:           # build_id (immutable content), so the size gate is safe and
   142:           # dedups the upload across Pis on the same build.
   143:           ansible.builtin.include_tasks: ../armbian/transport/upload_file.yml
   144:           vars:
   145:             _upload_local_src: "{{ rpi_tftp_cache_dir }}/{{ inventory_hostname }}/{{ item }}"
   146:             _upload_remote_path: "{{ _shared_dir }}/{{ item }}"
   147:             _upload_req_filename: "{{ rpi_tftp_prefix }}/{{ item }}"
   148:             _upload_req_filename_is_regex: false
   149:           loop: "{{ rpi_tftp_assets }}"
   150: 
   151:         - name: Prune shared build dirs no longer referenced by any Pi of this model
   152:           community.routeros.command:
   153:             commands:
   154:               - >-
   155:                 /file remove
   156:                 [find where name~"^{{ rpi_tftp_flash_dir }}/shared/{{ rpi_board_model }}/"
   157:                 and !(name~"({{ _active_builds | join('|') }})")]
   158:           register: _prune
   159:           retries: 3
   160:           delay: 5
   161:           until: _prune is succeeded
   162:           # Unconditional remove — RouterOS gives no removed-count back,
   163:           # so report changed rather than hide real mutations from AAP
   164:           # run summaries.
   165:           changed_when: true
   166: 
   167:         - name: Verify /ip tftp rows landed (plumbing check)
   168:           ansible.builtin.include_tasks: transport/plumbing_check.yml

review_question: Does this playbook have harmful dependency coupling?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: - hosts: all
     3:   become: yes
     4:   tasks:
     5:     - name: Check if systemd service exists
     6:       ansible.builtin.stat:
     7:         path: "/etc/systemd/system/{{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}.service"
     8:       register: service_file
     9: 
    10:     - name: Fail if service not installed
    11:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    12:         msg: "Hermes service not installed. Run 'clawctl agent install --type hermes ...' first."
    13:       when: not service_file.stat.exists
    14: 
    15:     # Re-render the unit (idempotent) so changes to ExecStart / WorkingDirectory
    16:     # via a clawctl upgrade are picked up without forcing a full reinstall. The
    17:     # `Also=` directive on this unit (not the dashboard unit) is intentional
    18:     # — see install.yaml comments / ATX W1.
    19:     - name: Sync systemd service file
    20:       ansible.builtin.copy:
    21:         dest: "/etc/systemd/system/{{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}.service"
    22:         content: |
    23:           [Unit]
    24:           Description=Hermes AI Agent ({{ agent_name }})
    25:           After=network.target
    26: 
    27:           [Service]
    28:           Type=simple
    29:           User={{ agent_name }}
    30:           WorkingDirectory=/home/{{ agent_name }}/.hermes
    31:           EnvironmentFile=/home/{{ agent_name }}/.hermes/.env
    32:           # PATH includes ~/.local/bin so subprocesses spawned by the gateway
    33:           # (notably the kanban dispatcher's `subprocess.run(["hermes", ...])`
    34:           # bare-name lookup) can resolve the hermes CLI without venv activation.
    35:           # Placed AFTER EnvironmentFile= so the unit-file value always wins
    36:           # over any PATH= an operator might add to .hermes/.env.
    37:           Environment=PATH=/home/{{ agent_name }}/.local/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
    38:           ExecStart=/home/{{ agent_name }}/.local/bin/hermes gateway run
    39:           Restart=on-failure
    40:           RestartSec=5
    41: 
    42:           [Install]
    43:           WantedBy=multi-user.target
    44:           Also={{ agent_type }}-dashboard-{{ agent_name }}.service
    45:         mode: "0644"
    46:       no_log: true
    47:       register: service_file_changed
    48: 
    49:     - name: Reload systemd if service file changed
    50:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
    51:         daemon_reload: yes
    52:       when: service_file_changed.changed
    53: 
    54:     # Re-render the dashboard unit (issue #478 phase 2). `dashboard_port` is
    55:     # passed from lifecycle.py via hosts.json.agents.<name>.config.dashboard.
    56:     # Re-rendering here keeps the unit in sync if a future clawctl upgrade
    57:     # changes the ExecStart shape without forcing a full re-install. The
    58:     # `when:` guard lets agents installed before this change continue to
    59:     # start (the dashboard unit just stays absent).
    60:     - name: Sync dashboard systemd service file
    61:       ansible.builtin.copy:
    62:         dest: "/etc/systemd/system/{{ agent_type }}-dashboard-{{ agent_name }}.service"
    63:         content: |
    64:           [Unit]
    65:           Description=Hermes Dashboard ({{ agent_name }})
    66:           After=network.target
    67:           PartOf={{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}.service
    68: 
    69:           [Service]
    70:           Type=simple
    71:           User={{ agent_name }}
    72:           WorkingDirectory=/home/{{ agent_name }}/.hermes
    73:           EnvironmentFile=/home/{{ agent_name }}/.hermes/.env
    74:           Environment=HERMES_DASHBOARD_TUI=1
    75:           ExecStart=/home/{{ agent_name }}/.local/bin/hermes dashboard --host 127.0.0.1 --port {{ dashboard_port }} --no-open --tui
    76:           Restart=on-failure
    77:           RestartSec=5
    78: 
    79:           [Install]
    80:           WantedBy=multi-user.target
    81:         mode: "0644"
    82:       no_log: true
    83:       register: dashboard_file_changed
    84:       when: dashboard_port is defined and (dashboard_port | string) | length > 0
    85: 
    86:     - name: Reload systemd if dashboard file changed
    87:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
    88:         daemon_reload: yes
    89:       when:
    90:         - dashboard_file_changed is defined
    91:         - dashboard_file_changed.changed | default(false)
    92: 
    93:     - name: Start hermes service
    94:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
    95:         name: "{{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}"
    96:         state: started
    97:         enabled: yes
    98:         daemon_reload: yes
    99:       register: start_result
   100: 
   101:     # Enable + start the dashboard companion unit (idempotent). PartOf in the
   102:     # unit file propagates stop/restart from the gateway, but `enable` and
   103:     # the initial `start` still have to be explicit. Skipped silently when
   104:     # the unit file is absent (legacy agents installed before this change).
   105:     - name: Check if dashboard systemd unit exists
   106:       ansible.builtin.stat:
   107:         path: "/etc/systemd/system/{{ agent_type }}-dashboard-{{ agent_name }}.service"
   108:       register: dashboard_unit_file
   109: 
   110:     - name: Start hermes dashboard service
   111:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
   112:         name: "{{ agent_type }}-dashboard-{{ agent_name }}"
   113:         state: started
   114:         enabled: yes
   115:         daemon_reload: yes
   116:       when: dashboard_unit_file.stat.exists
   117: 
   118:     # Brief settle window so systemd has time to either reach `active` or
   119:     # crash through `Restart=on-failure` cycles. Without this, ActiveState can
   120:     # still read `activating` when we immediately query it.
   121:     - name: Pause briefly to let service reach steady state
   122:       ansible.builtin.pause:
   123:         seconds: 3
   124: 
   125:     - name: Capture service active state
   126:       ansible.builtin.systemd:
   127:         name: "{{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}"
   128:       register: service_status
   129: 
   130:     - name: Display service state
   131:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   132:         msg: >-
   133:           Hermes service {{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }} is
   134:           {{ service_status.status.ActiveState }}
   135:           (sub-state: {{ service_status.status.SubState }}).
   136: 
   137:     # Fail loudly if the unit is not running. Previously the playbook
   138:     # reported success regardless of ActiveState, so the Python lifecycle
   139:     # layer wrote runtime.status='running' even when the service had exited
   140:     # with rc=1. This caused state divergence between clawctl and systemd.
   141:     - name: Fail if service is not active
   142:       ansible.builtin.fail:
   143:         msg: >-
   144:           Hermes service {{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }} failed to reach
   145:           'active' state (currently
   146:           {{ service_status.status.ActiveState }}/{{ service_status.status.SubState }}).
   147:           Inspect logs with:
   148:             sudo journalctl -u {{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }} -n 100 --no-pager
   149:           Common cause: ~/.hermes/.env is missing required provider credentials.
   150:           Run `clawctl agent configure {{ agent_name }}` to provision a provider.
   151:       when: service_status.status.ActiveState not in ['active', 'activating']
